reason: The hypothesis relies on specific claims about thermal gradients, domain wall pinning, and the effect of conductive interlayers on magnetocaloric performance in FeMnNiGeSi. The cited evidence (E1, E2) only describes thermal expansion measurement of a different HEA and a general thermal conductivity measurement technique, providing no support for any of these key premises.
premises: Local thermal gradients in thin films cause domain wall pinning and increase hysteresis during magnetic cycling
Introducing high-conductivity interlayers (e.g., Cu) in a multilayer stack enhances heat transfer and reduces thermal gradients
